name: A Nonempty Reduction Can Lose a Prescribed Peeling Endpoint
statement: There is an ample family $Y$ with $579$ concepts, isometric dimension $13$, and VC dimension $4$ that peels to a marked root $r$, while its nonempty one-coordinate reduction is the $289$-concept rooted factor $B$ and cannot peel to the projected root $29$. The full fibre through $r$ is present. The only corners of $Y$ are $(157,0)$ and $(29,1)$, and every peeling ending at $r=(29,0)$ starts by deleting $(29,1)$. VC dimension four is the least possible for prescribed-endpoint failure under a nonempty reduction.
proof: Let $M=B\cup\{157\}$ be the certified support-four endpoint repair and set $Y=(M\times\{0\})\cup(B\times\{1\})$. The peripheral-expansion shadow formula gives order $579$, dimension $13$, and VC dimension four. Clearing the upper copy of $B$ and then peeling $M$ to $29$ makes $Y$ peel to $r$, while the reduction is exactly $B$, whose unique corner $29$ must be deleted first and hence cannot be retained as an endpoint. Direct corner-cube inspection leaves only $(157,0)$ and $(29,1)$. Deleting the former produces $B\square Q_1$, whose root-containing restriction is the root-negative $B$, forcing every root-ending order to start with the latter. Finally, a reduction on a nonempty coordinate set lowers VC dimension by at least its size; below VC dimension four the reduction has VC dimension at most two and therefore peels to every prescribed concept.
